entries.title: Seed Memory Tensor RT Provisional Induction
entries.purpose: Introduce the memory tensor array concept as a governed provisional induction with explicit routing into mathematics and neuroscience.
entries.core_claim: A person's memory may be modeled as a tensor array of gradients, where recall is not retrieval of a stored object but a local traversal and resolution conditioned by orientation, slice trajectory, and implied memory prompts.

rt_position.epistemic_access: RT is inferred through local comparisons, not exhausted by them.

terms.TA: Tensor Array: the person's entire memory RT represented as gradients.
terms.m: Implied memory: the recall target induced by a question or prompt.
terms.confidence: The practical experience that a gradient resolution feels like the right recall.

formal_seed.interpretation: Local conditioned recall comparisons provide inferential access to RT.

implementation_notes.math_track: Define TA, gradient, orientation, slice, trajectory, and comparison operators.
implementation_notes.neuroscience_track: Map cautiously to distributed memory, cue-dependent recall, attractor stabilization, and confidence signals.
implementation_notes.simulation_track: Prototype a minimal tensor-gradient recall model before making biological claims.

constraints: Do not claim literal neural tensors have been proven.
Do not equate local confidence with historical correctness.
Do not treat RT as an output of the comparison; comparison occurs within RT.
notes: Preserved as a provisional seed only.
Routes into mathematics and neuroscience were split into separate wired provisional tracks.
The seed's RT wording remains under governance review against live RT/Core usage.
